newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Better Western tea prices fall at Colombo auction.
newsitem.headline: Better Western tea prices fall at Colombo auction.

text.p: Prices of better Western teas fell sharply at the Colombo auction because of lower quality but low growns did well, brokers said on Wednesday.

"Most Western high-priced teas came down by about seven or eight rupees following quality," said Yshan Fernando of Eastern Brokers. "Low growns, sold on Tuesday, did exceptionally well, like last week."
Last week's low grown average auction price was a record 133.86 rupees, bettering the previous high of 128.86 rupees set on October 16, 1996, he said.
Brokers Forbes and Walker said there was fair demand for low growns from the traditional Commonwealth of Independent States and Middle East markets.
But they said the anticipated average auction price for the six million kg on offer fell to 118.50 rupees ($2.03) from 119.24 last week.
The next auction is on June 3-4 when six million kg will be on offer. ($1=58.44 rupees)
